checks.evidence: Home is organized into hero, debate, recent, topics, norms and how-to-read sections.
checks.recommendation: Keep the home structured by sections instead of shortcuts.

checks.evidence: Home exposes a natural-language search form for real agenda items.
checks.recommendation: Keep the first action centered on a plain-language question.

checks.evidence: Home does not render quick-access chips below the search box.
checks.recommendation: Organize discovery through sections, not highlighted shortcut chips.

checks.evidence: Search results can explain why a proposal matched and support shareable query URLs.
checks.recommendation: Keep natural-language search connected to concrete changes, not only proposal titles.

checks.evidence: The productive UI seed uses official Senate agenda items and no longer exposes fictional or Diputados data in this vertical slice.
checks.recommendation: Keep test/demo data out of the user-facing home.

checks.evidence: Recent changes has an explicit empty state instead of invented data.
checks.recommendation: Keep empty states honest while data is incomplete.

checks.evidence: The screen gives a plain summary before the article-by-article diff.
checks.recommendation: Do not lead with dense legal text.

checks.evidence: Important norms is visually marked as reference, not the main product flow.
checks.recommendation: Keep norms below debate/recent changes and visually quieter.

checks.evidence: The UI separates affected topics from impacted groups.
checks.recommendation: Keep topics and groups visible before detailed legal comparison.

checks.evidence: Each change has current and proposed text in separate blocks.
checks.recommendation: Preserve access to both legal texts in every diff item.

checks.evidence: Every diff renders what changes and what it means.
checks.recommendation: Do not collapse practical impact into technical legal labels.

checks.evidence: Source, data status, scope and legal warning are rendered.
checks.recommendation: Keep trust metadata visible without requiring a technical view.

checks.evidence: Agenda metadata and original source link fields are visible in the detail flow.
checks.recommendation: Keep agenda/citation/original text source states separate.

checks.evidence: Legal update dates are formatted without local timezone day drift.
checks.recommendation: Keep date-only legal metadata stable across locales.

checks.evidence: Each diff renders sources for current and proposed versions.
checks.recommendation: Every diff must expose both original source states.

checks.evidence: Missing original links are explicit and visible.
checks.recommendation: Never hide or invent missing original source links.

checks.evidence: The UI has an explicit empty state for proposals without loaded legal texts.
checks.recommendation: Do not show article-level comparisons until source texts are loaded.

checks.evidence: The interface warns that it is not personalized legal advice.
checks.recommendation: Avoid imperative advice for a user's individual situation.

checks.evidence: The static page has language, landmarks, hidden labels and one H1.
checks.recommendation: Keep labels and document structure explicit as the UI grows.

checks.evidence: How-to-read section is brief and uses the four expected concepts.
checks.recommendation: Keep the explanation short, visual and useful.

checks.evidence: CSS defines responsive breakpoints and collapses the diff layout.
checks.recommendation: Verify real mobile screenshots before production announcements.

checks.evidence: Typography avoids negative letter spacing and viewport-scaled font sizes.
checks.recommendation: Use fixed/rem sizes and responsive containers instead of viewport font scaling.

checks.evidence: The static shell does not depend on third-party runtime assets.
checks.recommendation: Keep the MVP shell self-contained for Cloudflare Pages.

checks.evidence: A separate operational page can show processor heartbeats and queue status without cluttering the public legal-diff home.
checks.recommendation: Keep processor controls out of the public UX; expose only read-only operational state.
